title: finding(tests): the `object-calendar` annotation pin asserts a total property with a column-0-anchored regex, so the one unannotated literal on its own input page has always been invisible to it
body:
Found while re-scoping objectui#7311. That card's dispatch stopped on a falsified premise, and this is why the defect it is about survived a pin written to catch exactly it.

## What

`packages/types/src/__tests__/object-calendar-record-source-7313.test.ts:485`-`:486`, verbatim on `main` at `72f55c9ec`:

```js
    // No bare `object-calendar` literal is left unannotated on the page.
    expect(page.match(/^const \w+ = \{\n\s+type: 'object-calendar'/gm)).toBeNull();
```

The comment states a **total** property over the page. The regex checks something much narrower, and is blind in **two independent ways**:

1. **The caret with the `m` flag anchors at column 0.** A literal declared inside a function is indented, so the pattern cannot see it at all.
2. **The pattern requires `type: 'object-calendar'` to be the literal's FIRST member.** A literal that omits the discriminant entirely — the actual failure mode the page's own prose is about — matches nothing, whatever its indentation.

Either one alone defeats the stated claim. `toBeNull()` then reads as a pass, and a pass on an assertion that cannot fail is not a measurement.

## The live specimen is on the page this very pin reads

`content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx`, the **Direct Component Usage** block:

```
  const schema = {
    objectName: 'events',
    calendar: { startDateField: 'startDate', titleField: 'title' }
  };
```

Indented inside `function MyObjectCalendar`, and carrying no `type` member. It is **the only unannotated `object-calendar` literal left on the page** — measured, the page carries ten-plus annotated ones: `const schema: ObjectCalendarSchema = {` at lines 195 and 212, then `fieldMappedCalendar` / `objectProviderCalendar` / `valueProviderCalendar` / `eventClickCalendar` / `dateClickCalendar` / `appointmentCalendar` / `eventCalendar` at 315, 334, 349, 419, 439, 460, 480, plus `const schema: CalendarViewSchema = {` at 114.

⇒ The pin was written as objectui#7313's completion signal, it has been green ever since, and the one literal that would falsify its stated claim has been sitting in its own input the whole time.

## Probe

Run the same regex over two samples: a column-0 `const x = {` whose first member is the discriminant **matches**; the same text indented by two spaces returns **null**. Then run it over the real page: null, while the Direct Component Usage block is present and unannotated.

## Why this is the declaration's half

The two assertions above it (lines 483-484) are `toContain` checks on exact strings and are honest — they name two specific consts and verify those two carry the annotation. It is only the third line, the one that generalises, that overclaims. The repair is to make the check match the sentence, or to make the sentence match the check; it is not to delete either.

## Not asserted here

⛔ Whether any OTHER page in `content/docs/**` carries an unannotated `object-calendar` literal is **not measured** — this card read the one page the pin reads. ⛔ Whether the same column-0-anchor shape appears in sibling pins is also not measured; if a grader wants that sweep it is a separate, wider question.

Refs: objectui#7311 (the card whose dispatch surfaced this) - objectui#7313 (the card this pin was written for).
